listingTitle: Use a supported Spring async return type
title: Use a supported Spring async return type
why: Spring asynchronous methods require void or a Future-compatible return type; an unsupported declared return type can fail when asynchronous advice is applied.
suggestion: Return void, Future, CompletableFuture, or a supported Future subtype, and preserve asynchronous failure observation where needed.
limitations: High-confidence findings bind canonical method- or class-level Async through explicit imports, wildcard imports, or fully qualified names. Managed-class evidence is limited to top-level nonabstract classes with canonical stereotypes or an unambiguous Bean return type in a statically identified Spring module.

Void, Future, CompletableFuture, and recognizable Future subtypes are accepted. Rejections are limited to primitives, arrays, and bound known JDK/reactor types; unknown user types and type parameters are not assumed unsupported. Private and static methods are excluded because ordinary proxy advice cannot intercept them. This is a bounded Java index, not compiler type resolution.
Dynamic Gradle configuration, dependency aliases, unresolved Maven properties, profile activation, remote parent inheritance, custom meta-annotations, and Kotlin or Groovy source are not resolved.
